Notes

The figures are kept apart from the drawing on purpose: the chart is a picture, and the first tab holds what it shows. A bead, such as ex-1a2b, is named whole. The source of one made-up hash is example.com, and here it is with no break to take: 9f31c0a4e7b2d85a6c19f0e3b7d4a2c85e61f9d0b3a7c4e28d5f16a09b3c7e41.

  • A list item stays in the column, however long its words run on without a break, as this one does for the sake of the test.
  • A second item, with inline code in it.
A quotation reads quieter than the text around it.
sort -k2,2 -n landed.tsv | awk '{ sum += $2 } END { print sum / NR, "beads a day, over the whole of these two weeks, on a line long enough to scroll" }'

What a run adds

With scripts off this page reads whole: the tabs above stack as three sections and nothing waits behind a hover. Run, it adds the tab bar, and a mark in either chart lights with its row in the first tab.
